description: Single source of truth for Spring Boot + JPA guardrail rules. Consumed by hooks/jpa-guardrail.py (runtime advisories) and agents/springboot-reviewer.md (review checklist). One rule defined here updates both.

rules.title: Entity missing @Version (no optimistic locking)
rules.advisory: Entity has no @Version field. Concurrent updates can silently overwrite each other (lost-update). Add optimistic locking unless intentionally omitted.
rules.fixHint: Add `@Version private Long version;` to the entity (or document why optimistic locking is not needed).

rules.title: Entity equals/hashCode must use a stable business key, not the generated @Id

match.note: Whether equals/hashCode is safe depends on WHICH field it uses — a business key/UUID (correct) vs the generated @Id (wrong). A line-level regex cannot tell these apart, so it would also flag correct-by-default entities (e.g. the jpa-entity scaffold). The reviewer reads the equals body and judges; the hook stays out of it.

rules.advisory: equals()/hashCode() based on a generated @Id is unsafe before the entity is persisted (id is null) and breaks Set/Map membership. Use a stable business key or an assigned UUID.
rules.fixHint: Base equals/hashCode on an immutable business key (e.g. a natural key or a UUID assigned at construction), not the generated @Id.

rules.title: @Transactional on a non-public method (Spring AOP won't proxy it)
rules.advisory: @Transactional on a private/protected/static method is silently ignored — Spring's proxy only advises public methods invoked from another bean. The transaction will NOT start.
rules.fixHint: Make the method public and call it from a different bean, or move the transactional boundary to a public service method.

rules.title: Controller returns a JPA entity instead of a DTO

match.note: Cross-file: a @RestController method whose return type is a class annotated @Entity. Requires resolving types across files — handled by the reviewer agent, not the line-level hook.

rules.advisory: Returning a JPA entity from a controller leaks the persistence model to the API and risks LazyInitializationException during serialization. Map to a DTO.
rules.fixHint: Introduce a response DTO and map the entity to it in the service or a mapper; never serialize the entity directly.

rules.title: Possible N+1 — repository call inside a loop
rules.advisory: A repository call appears inside a loop — likely an N+1 query pattern. Each iteration may hit the database.
rules.fixHint: Fetch in one query: a JOIN FETCH / @EntityGraph, a batch findAllById, or @BatchSize. Verify whether this loop actually issues per-row queries.

rules.title: Query built by string concatenation (injection risk)
rules.advisory: A JPQL/native query is assembled with string concatenation. This is an injection vector and defeats query plan caching.
rules.fixHint: Use bind parameters (`:name` with @Param, or positional `?1`) — never concatenate user input into a query string.

rules.title: FetchType.EAGER on an association (over-fetching / N+1 source)
rules.advisory: FetchType.EAGER loads the association on every query — over-fetching and a frequent N+1 source. Note @ManyToOne/@OneToOne default to EAGER, so set fetch explicitly. Prefer LAZY and fetch on demand.
rules.fixHint: Use fetch = FetchType.LAZY; load the association when needed via a JOIN FETCH query or @EntityGraph.

rules.title: CascadeType.ALL cascades remove across associations
rules.advisory: CascadeType.ALL implicitly includes REMOVE, so deleting (or detaching) the parent cascades into the children and can wipe an entire object graph unintentionally. Cascade only inside an aggregate boundary you fully own. (orphanRemoval=true with cascade={PERSIST,MERGE} is the standard aggregate pattern and is intentionally NOT flagged.)
rules.fixHint: Cascade explicitly (e.g. {PERSIST, MERGE}) and only within an aggregate root; avoid CascadeType.ALL / REMOVE across entity boundaries.

rules.title: GenerationType.IDENTITY disables JDBC batch inserts
rules.advisory: GenerationType.IDENTITY disables JDBC batch inserts (Hibernate must read each generated key per row), hurting bulk-insert throughput. Prefer SEQUENCE with a pooled allocator.
rules.fixHint: Use @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.SEQUENCE, generator = "...") + @SequenceGenerator(allocationSize = 50) for batchable inserts.

rules.title: Open Session In View enabled (lazy loads leak into the view layer)
rules.advisory: spring.jpa.open-in-view=true keeps the persistence context open through view rendering, hiding lazy-loading queries in the controller/serialization layer and causing surprise N+1. Disable it and fetch explicitly in the service layer.
rules.fixHint: Set spring.jpa.open-in-view=false and load required associations in the service (JOIN FETCH / @EntityGraph / DTO projection).

rules.title: Read path returns full entities where a DTO/interface projection would fit

match.note: Whether a read query should return a DTO/interface projection instead of a full entity depends on how the result is consumed downstream (serialized to the API, only a few columns used, lazy associations later touched). That is a cross-file judgement the reviewer makes, not a line-level regex — so the hook stays out of it.

rules.advisory: This read path loads full entities where a DTO or interface projection would fetch exactly the needed columns in a single query, avoiding over-fetching and lazy-loading surprises.
rules.fixHint: Return a Spring Data interface projection or a JPQL constructor-expression DTO for read-only queries; see springboot-conventions/references/persistence.md (jpa-dto-projection).

rules.title: @RequestBody/@ModelAttribute parameter not validated with @Valid
rules.advisory: @RequestBody/@ModelAttribute parameter is not validated with @Valid — Bean Validation constraints on the DTO are skipped and invalid input reaches the service layer.
rules.fixHint: Add @Valid (or @Validated for group validation): create(@Valid @RequestBody CreateDto dto).
